W1.what: per-reference exponent of log flips on log KL (configs with 1e-3 < KL < 2, simulated configs only)

W2.pass_if: within [0.99, 1.25], the 5th-95th percentile band of the 54 published per-reference medians
W2.what: per-reference median flips/TV over simulated configs

W3.pass_if: >= 90% of configurations within [0.89, 1.29], the central 95% of the 802 published configurations

W4.what: flips/TV of each real-kernel (nf4, int8, fp8) and released-weight checkpoint

W5.pass_if: for every model, the median absolute relative error of the TV route is below that of the KL route, and the TV route's median error is at most 10%
W5.what: cross-corpus transfer within a model: predict corpus B's per-config flips from corpus A, for every ordered pair (A, B) of corpora

exclusions: a run whose KL or TV is not finite is reported as a kernel failure and excluded from W1-W5
released-weight checkpoints are dequantized into bf16 (published weights, simulated kernel); nf4/int8/fp8 run the real kernels
a model that cannot be loaded is reported and dropped; the criteria stay unchanged for the others
models_note: none is among the 19 models of the main study (Qwen2.5 7B and 72B are; 14B is not)
registered_before: any reference corpus or score of the models below was generated
scoring: teacher forcing on the dense model's greedy references, fp32 output head, top-64 plus tail, as in the main study
title: In-the-wild test: new models, released checkpoints and real kernels
